newsitem.title: USA: Edison Intl Mission unit continues to grow.
newsitem.headline: Edison Intl Mission unit continues to grow.

text.p: Growth at Edison International's Mission Energy unit continued to shore up the company's results in the first quarter, when it's Southern California Edison Co (SCE) saw a drop in revenue.
The company on Thursday reported earnings for the first quarter of 1997 of 35 cents per share, compared with 38 cents for the same period last year.

The electric utility contributed earnings of 27 cents a share, down four cents from the same period last year due to a revised ratemaking plan for nuclear facilities which called for accelerated recovery of the investments in exchange for a lower authorized rate of return.
SCE's nuclear assets are now earning an annual return on equity of about 7 percent, compared to 11.6 percent in the first quarter of 1996.
Also, during the first quarter of 1997, a unit at the San Onofre nuclear plant was out of service for an extended refueling outage.
But the decrease in revenue associated with the outage was offset by a reduction in costs from continuing operations and the results of EIX's continuing share repurchase program, the company said.
Earnings from Mission Energy, which develops independent power projects worldwide, were up in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the first quarter of 1996, the company reported.

Earnings from Edison Capital and Mission Land Co were described as flat vs the year-ago quarter, while the combined earnings of Mission, Edison Capital and Mission Land were 10 cents a share in the first quarter, up from 7 cents.

The increase was primarily due to earnings contributed by Mission's foreign projects, specifically First Hydro, which benefited from higher energy prices in Britain and increased utilization, and Kwinana, a project in Australia which began commercial operation in December, 1996.
